summary: There are many ways to say "I will be a nazir." This mishnah lists words that make a person a nazir, even when he does not say the word "nazir" exactly.
stIntro: One becomes a nazirite by taking a nazirite vow, in which he simply declares himself a nazirite, as detailed in the Torah (Numbers 6:1–21). Additionally,

chunks.en: All the different ways of saying nezirus count like nezirus.
chunks.st: all substitutes for the language of nazirite vows are like nazirite vows and are binding.
chunks.stMore: Furthermore, intimations of nazirite vows, i.e., incomplete statements that are understood from context to be meant as nazirite vows, are considered binding nazirite vows. Consequently,

words.note: Nezirus: a promise to be a nazir, who may not drink wine, cut his hair, or become tamei from a dead person.

chunks.en: If someone says, "I will be,"
chunks.explain: He says it when a nazir passes by, and means "I will be like him."
chunks.st: one who says: I will be, without further clarification,

chunks.en: he is a nazir.
chunks.st: is a nazirite, as this is his implied intention.

chunks.en: Or if he says, "I will be beautiful," he is a nazir.
chunks.explain: He holds his hair and means he will grow it long like a nazir.
chunks.st: Or, if he said: I will be beautiful, he is a nazirite.
chunks.stMore: The substitutes for the language of nazirite vows are as follows:

chunks.en: If he says, "nazik," "naziach," or "paziach,"
chunks.st: If one says: I will be a nazik, a nazi’aḥ, or a pazi’aḥ,

words.note: Words from other languages that sound like "nazir."

chunks.en: he is a nazir.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite.

chunks.en: If he says, "I am like this one,"
chunks.explain: He points to a nazir near him.
chunks.st: If one says: I am hereby like this,

chunks.en: or "I will curl my hair,"
chunks.st: I am hereby a hair curler,

chunks.en: or "I am growing my hair,"
chunks.st: I am hereby growing my hair;

chunks.en: or "I must let my hair grow long,"
chunks.st: or: It is incumbent upon me to grow long hair,

chunks.en: he is a nazir.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite.

chunks.en: If he says, "I must bring birds,"
chunks.explain: A nazir who becomes tamei brings two birds as korbanos.
chunks.st: If one says: An obligation is hereby incumbent upon me with regard to birds,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says he is a nazir.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says: He is a nazirite.
chunks.stMore: A nazirite brings two bird-offerings if he inadvertently becomes ritually impure from a corpse (Numbers 6:10), and it is understood that the individual used this indirect phrase to take a vow of naziriteship.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Sages say:

chunks.en: he is not a nazir.
chunks.st: He is not a nazirite.

summary: If someone says he will be a nazir only from one thing, like grape seeds, he becomes a full nazir anyway. The mishnah also teaches about a "nazir like Shimshon," and how he is different from a nazir forever.

chunks.en: If someone says, "I am a nazir from grape seeds,"
chunks.st: If one said: I am hereby a nazirite and therefore will refrain from grape seeds, or:

chunks.en: or "from grape skins,"
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite and therefore will refrain from grape skins, or:

chunks.en: or "from shaving,"
chunks.st: From shaving, or:

chunks.en: or "from becoming tamei,"
chunks.st: From impurity,

chunks.en: he is a nazir,
chunks.st: he is a nazirite.

chunks.en: and all the rules of nezirus are on him.
chunks.st: And all details of naziriteship are incumbent upon him.
chunks.stMore: Not only does the prohibition he mentioned take effect, he is bound by all of the strictures of naziriteship.

chunks.en: If he says, "I am like Shimshon,"
chunks.st: If one said: I am hereby like Samson,

words.note: A strong hero in Tanach, who was a nazir all his life.

chunks.en: "like the son of Manoach,"
chunks.st: like the son of Manoah,

chunks.en: "like the husband of Delilah,"
chunks.st: like the husband of Delilah,

chunks.en: "like the one who pulled out the doors of Azah,"
chunks.st: like the one who tore off the doors of Gaza,

chunks.en: "like the one whose eyes the Pelishtim poked out,"
chunks.st: like the one whose eyes were gouged out by the Philistines,

chunks.en: he is a "nazir like Shimshon."
chunks.st: he is a nazirite like Samson,
chunks.stMore: whose halakhot are explained in the next mishna (see Judges, chapters 13–16).

chunks.he: מַה בֵּין נְזִיר עוֹלָם לִנְזִיר שִׁמְשׁוֹן.
chunks.en: What is the difference between a nazir forever and a nazir like Shimshon?
chunks.st: What is the difference between a permanent nazirite and a nazirite like Samson, both of whom remain nazirites forever?

chunks.en: A nazir forever:
chunks.st: In the case of a permanent nazirite,

chunks.en: if his hair gets too heavy,
chunks.st: if his hair grows too heavy for him,

chunks.en: he makes it lighter with a razor, and brings three animals as korbanos.
chunks.st: he lightens it by cutting some hair with a razor, and he then brings three animals
chunks.stMore: as a sin-offering, a burnt-offering, and a peace-offering, like one who completes his term of naziriteship.

chunks.en: And if he becomes tamei,
chunks.st: And if he becomes ritually impure,

chunks.en: he brings the korban for tumah.
chunks.st: he brings the offering for impurity
chunks.stMore: brought by a regular nazirite who became impure.

chunks.en: A nazir like Shimshon:
chunks.st: By contrast, in the case of a nazirite like Samson,

chunks.en: if his hair gets heavy,
chunks.st: if his hair grows heavy

chunks.en: he may not make it lighter.
chunks.st: he may not lighten it,
chunks.stMore: since he is entirely prohibited from cutting his hair.

chunks.en: And if he becomes tamei,
chunks.st: And if he becomes impure,

chunks.en: he does not bring a korban for tumah.
chunks.st: he does not bring an offering for impurity.

summary: If someone says "I am a nazir" without saying for how long, he is a nazir for thirty days. The mishnah teaches what happens if he adds words like "big," "one day," or "one hour."

chunks.en: Plain nezirus, with no time said, is thirty days.
chunks.st: In the case of unspecified naziriteship, where one does not state how long he wishes to be a nazirite, the term lasts for thirty days.

chunks.en: If he says, "I am a nazir for one big time,"
chunks.st: If one said: I am hereby a nazirite for one long term,

chunks.en: or "I am a nazir for one small time,"
chunks.st: or: I am hereby a nazirite for one short term,

chunks.en: or even "from here until the end of the world,"
chunks.st: or even if one said: I am hereby a nazirite from now until the end of the world,

chunks.en: he is a nazir for thirty days.
chunks.st: in all these cases he is a nazirite for thirty days.

chunks.en: If he says, "I am a nazir and one day,"
chunks.st: If one said: I am hereby a nazirite and one day,

chunks.en: or "I am a nazir and one hour,"
chunks.st: or: I am hereby a nazirite and one hour,

chunks.en: or "I am a nazir one and a half times,"
chunks.st: or: I am hereby a nazirite for one and a half,

chunks.en: he is a nazir two times.
chunks.explain: Each time of nezirus is at least thirty days.
chunks.st: he becomes a nazirite for two
chunks.stMore: consecutive terms of naziriteship. When he says: I am hereby a nazirite, he accepts upon himself one thirty-day term of naziriteship. When he subsequently adds an additional amount of time, e.g., an extra day, he thereby accepts upon himself an additional term of naziriteship, and the minimal term of naziriteship is thirty days.

chunks.he: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם וְשָׁעָה אֶחָת,
chunks.en: If he says, "I am a nazir for thirty days and one hour,"
chunks.st: One who says: I am hereby a nazirite for thirty days and one hour,

chunks.en: he is a nazir for thirty-one days,
chunks.st: becomes a nazirite for thirty-one days,

chunks.en: because we don't make nezirus for hours.
chunks.st: as there is no naziriteship for hours but only for full days.

summary: If someone says he is a nazir "like the hair of my head," he is a nazir forever. Rebbi and the first Tanna argue whether he cuts his hair every thirty days.

chunks.en: If he says, "I am a nazir like the hair of my head,"
chunks.st: If one says: I am hereby a nazirite like the hair of my head,

chunks.en: or "like the dust of the earth,"
chunks.st: or: Like the dust of the earth,

chunks.en: or "like the sand of the sea,"
chunks.st: or: Like the sand of the sea,

chunks.en: he is a nazir forever,
chunks.explain: Each hair counts as its own nezirus.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite forever.
chunks.stMore: He has accepted a separate term of naziriteship for every hair or particle of dust or sand, which in practice means that he will be a nazirite forever.

chunks.en: and he shaves his hair once every thirty days.
chunks.st: And he shaves his hair once every thirty days.

chunks.en: Rebbi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who put together the Mishnah.

chunks.he: אֵין זֶה מְגַלֵּחַ אַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם.
chunks.en: this one does not shave once every thirty days.
chunks.explain: For him it is one very long nezirus.
chunks.st: This nazirite does not shave his hair once every thirty days,
chunks.stMore: as he has accepted upon himself one long term of naziriteship lasting for as many days as there are hairs or particles of dust or sand.

chunks.en: So who is the one who shaves once every thirty days?
chunks.st: And who is the nazirite who shaves his hair once every thirty days?

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי נְזִירוּת כִּשְׂעַר רֹאשִׁי,
chunks.en: One who says, "I take on many nezirus times, like the hair of my head,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is hereby incumbent upon me to observe naziriteships like the hair of my head,

chunks.en: or "like the dust of the earth,"
chunks.st: or: Like the dust of the earth,

chunks.en: or "like the sand of the sea."
chunks.st: or: Like the sand of the sea.
chunks.stMore: Since he used the plural term naziriteships, it is clear that he is accepting distinct terms of naziriteship.

summary: If someone says he is a nazir "as much as fills a house" or "a basket," we ask him what he meant. If he meant nothing special, he is a nazir all his life.

chunks.en: If he says, "I am a nazir as much as fills the house,"
chunks.st: If one says: I am hereby a nazirite in accordance with the capacity of the house,

chunks.en: or "as much as fills the basket,"
chunks.st: or: The capacity of the basket,

chunks.en: we ask him what he meant.
chunks.st: one checks with him what he had in mind.

chunks.en: If he says, "I meant one big nezirus,"
chunks.st: If he said: My intention was to take a nazirite vow for one long term of naziriteship,

words.en: I vowed to be a nazir

chunks.en: he is a nazir for thirty days.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite for only thirty days,
chunks.stMore: in accordance with the ruling of the mishna that the words long or short are of no account when used in a nazirite vow (7a).

chunks.en: And if he says, "I just made a plain nezirus,"
chunks.st: And if he said: I took a nazirite vow without specification,
chunks.stMore: it is assumed that he meant to accept upon himself terms of naziriteship corresponding to the number of items that fit into the basket, and the smallest items normally placed in baskets are used for this evaluation.

words.en: I vowed to be a nazir

chunks.en: we look at the basket as if
chunks.st: Consequently, one views the basket as though it were

chunks.en: it is full of mustard seeds,
chunks.explain: Mustard seeds are tiny. Each seed counts as one nezirus.
chunks.st: full of mustard seeds, which are extremely small,

chunks.en: and he is a nazir all his life.
chunks.st: and he is a nazirite for his entire life.

summary: If someone says "I am a nazir from here until a certain place," we figure out how many days it takes to walk there.

chunks.he: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר מִכָּאן עַד מָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: If he says, "I am a nazir from here until a certain place,"
chunks.st: If one says: I am hereby a nazirite from here until such and such a place,

chunks.en: we figure out how many days it takes from here
chunks.st: one estimates how many days it takes to walk from here

chunks.en: to that place.
chunks.st: until such and such a place.

chunks.en: If it is less than thirty days,
chunks.st: If it is less than thirty days,

chunks.en: he is a nazir for thirty days.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite for thirty days,
chunks.stMore: since this is the minimum term of naziriteship.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if not,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if it takes more than thirty days to walk that distance,

chunks.en: he is a nazir for that number of days.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite in accordance with the number of days it takes to walk to that place.

summary: If someone says he is a nazir "like the number of days of the sun's year," he must keep 365 nezirus times, one after the other.

chunks.en: If he says, "I am a nazir like the number of days of the sun's year,"
chunks.st: If one says: I am hereby a nazirite in accordance with the number of days in a solar year,

chunks.en: he counts that many nezirus times, one for each day of the sun's year.
chunks.st: he counts 365 consecutive naziriteships, in accordance with the number of days in a solar year.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: There was a story like this.
chunks.st: There was an incident
chunks.stMore: where someone took this vow and observed 365 consecutive terms of naziriteship.

chunks.en: As soon as he finished, he died.
chunks.st: Once he completed all these terms of naziriteship, he died.
